resources.string: Put in front of every request, in every chat and every pipeline. The agent treats it as standing orders.
Low keeps the wording predictable and repetitive; high makes it varied and less literal.
How many candidate words stay in play at each step. Small is safer and blander; large lets rarer words through.
Keeps only the likeliest words that together add up to this share of the probability. Lower cuts more.
Pushes the model off words it has already used. Too high and it starts avoiding words the answer needs.
How much of the conversation the model sees at once. Larger remembers more of the thread and runs slower.
Recording stops on its own at this point and sends what it has.
Which chip runs the on-device model. NPU is fastest where it works; the app falls back on its own if it does not.
On, durable facts from your chats — names, preferences, project details — are saved and reused later.
Old memories get merged into shorter summaries once there are many. Frees room; loses the exact wording.
Long threads are summarised past the live window, so the agent keeps the gist instead of forgetting the start.
How many memories are pulled into a reply at most. More context, slower start, and more room for noise.
Higher recalls only close matches, so less is pulled in; lower recalls more, including memories that miss the point.
How fast old memories lose to new ones when both match. Short favours this week; long treats everything as current.
How old a memory must be before compaction may merge it. Fresher facts keep their exact wording until they pass it.
The ceiling on stored pieces. Reaching it starts a compaction pass, so it does nothing at all while compaction is switched off.
How large a thread grows before its older half is summarised. Lower compresses sooner and keeps less of the original wording.
How many recent messages stay word-for-word after a thread is summarised. Anything older survives only as the summary.
How many recent memories are written into the prompt\'s memory block. More recall, less room for everything else.
The model that turns text into the numbers memory search compares. Change it and recall stays poor until you re-embed by hand.
Every retrieval is written to the console — useful when answers cite the wrong thing, noisy otherwise.
Re-embed rebuilds every vector for the current model. Stay on this screen while it runs, and expect poor recall until it finishes.
How many levels of sub-pipeline a run may descend into before it is refused. Deeper composes more; shallow fails a runaway sooner.
When a model answers in the wrong shape, how many times it is shown its own output and asked again before the node gives up.
Which tool calls stop and wait for your approval. Never lets them all through, destructive ones too, unless you also block those.
On, a destructive tool call is refused outright rather than offered for approval, and the run sees it as a failed call.
On, no cloud provider can be reached even with a key saved. Only a model on this device, or Ollama on your own network, answers.
How long one tool call may take before it is abandoned. Short frees a stuck run sooner; long suits slow servers.
The largest single file the workspace accepts, for both writing one and reading one whole.
How much device storage the whole workspace may hold. A write that would push past it is refused rather than trimmed.
How much of a file one read may put in front of the model. The rest is cut, leaving room for the prompt and the thread.
How much of a web response reaches the model. Past it the body is cut and marked, so remote text cannot flood the context.
A notification arrives when a scheduled task finishes or fails, so a background result does not wait for you to open the app.
Which pipeline runs when you share text or a link into the app from somewhere else.
On, every share lands in one Shared chat. Off, each share opens its own, so the chat list grows with each one.
Which pipeline the Quick Settings tile runs when you tap it from the notification shade.
Other apps on this device can start a run — Tasker, MacroDroid, adb. Off, those requests are refused.
The only pipeline an outside app may start. Nothing else can be named in the request, whatever it asks for.
How stale a parked run may be and still resume. Past it the run is dropped, because its gathered context no longer holds.
How long a background run waits for you to approve a tool call. Unanswered past it, the run ends rather than waiting forever.
Off, nothing leaves the device. On, crashes and error-level log lines are sent — never your messages, files, prompts or keys.
How many past runs keep their step-by-step trace in a chat. Older traces are dropped; the messages themselves stay.
How long a trace is kept before it is dropped, whatever the per-chat count. Bounds what accumulates on disk.
